messages.subject: Determine optimal number of clusters with SSC
messages.subject_clean: Determine optimal number of clusters with SSC
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kylie,

I am trying to determine the optimal number of clusters according to the method you described in your paper "Probabilistic Segmentation of Mass Spectrometry..." 2016. You do that by performing unsupervised SSC with a variation of k and s and conclude, that the optimal number of cluster is depicted when starting from different k values the "number of clusters"-graphs intersect with each other. I was trying this method as well only using more than 2 starting k values. I observed that there are multiple intersections at different cluster numbers and s values. I am wondering how you would choose the optimal combination of k and s from these graphs and what would you rank higher: high s or high cluster number. Or is this approach with more than two k values not suitable? Attached you'll find the graphs of two samples.

Thank you!

messages.body_plain:
Hi Kylie,

I am working with a  data set with 5 merged files( run1, ... , run5) . Each previously
individual file contains 2 tissue sections (1 healthy, 1 tumor) with their added
diagnosis factor. I performed  cross
validation (PLS-DA) on the merged data set.

Now I would like to get a median value for the fitted scores from each individual tissue section ( run1_healthy, run1_tumor, run2_healthy, ... , run5_tumor)

As each sample contains scores from two samples, I am struggling
to get the fitted scores separated.

Is there a way to extract the values based on the diagnosis
factor assigned to the pixels.

Best wishes,

Uwe

messages.subject_clean: Extracting fitted scores from crossvalidation based on diagnosis factor
messages.body_plain:
Hi
I guess I found a way but it seems quite tedious:

run1_values<-as.data.frame(my_data@resultData$`run1`@resultData$`ncomp = 20`$fitted)
run1_values$diagnosis<-( my_data @resultData$ `run1`  @resultData$`ncomp = 20`$y)
summary( run1_values  [ run1_values $y=="healthy",])
summary( run1_values  [ run1_values $y=="tumor",])

maybe there is an easier way...

best wishes,
Uwe
